rules.title: Relocation Assistance Rent Offset Exemption
rules.requirement: Landlord may offset tenant's accumulated rent against any relocation assistance, except when relocation assistance is owed because termination of tenancy is required by governmental agency order to vacate or comply with an issued order for an unpermitted dwelling.

tenancy is required by a governmental agency order to vacate or comply with an issued
order for an unpermitted dwelling.

rule.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Evictions Under RSO & JCO
rule.requirement: All tenant not-at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with LAHD before evicting tenants from units covered by RSO or JCO. Failure to file the Declaration makes the eviction a violation of RSO or JCO.
rule.quoted_span: All tenant not-at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO.
rule.coverage_conditions: Unit subject to RSO or JCO; eviction for no-fault reason (owner/family occupancy, demolition, governmental order, HUD ownership, residential hotel conversion, affordable housing conversion, or condominium/commercial conversion)
rule.exemptions: Evicting resident manager to replace with another resident manager; evictions due to hazardous conditions from natural disaster not caused by landlord negligence
rule.sanctions: Failure to file Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD makes eviction a violation of RSO or JCO; tenant may raise non-payment as affirmative defense in possession action; tenant may file complaint with LAHD or seek private right of action

rule.title: Relocation Assistance Payment Timing and Filing Procedures
rule.requirement: Relocation assistance payment must be made available within 15 days of service of written notice of eviction. Notices to terminate tenancy can only be served after landlord files Declaration with LAHD. A copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after service. Landlord may elect to place funds in escrow account within 15-day period with disbursement within 3 working days of payment request.
rule.quoted_span: Payment shall be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction. Notices to terminate tenancy can only be served on the tenant after the landlord files the Declaration with LAHD, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after it is served. At the landlord's sole discretion and cost, the landlord may elect to pay the monetary relocation benefits through an escrow account.
rule.coverage_conditions: Unit subject to RSO or JCO; no-fault eviction with Declaration filed
rule.sanctions: Failure to comply with payment timing or filing procedures may result in tenant raising non-payment as affirmative defense and filing LAHD complaint or private action

field_evidence.quoted_span: Payment shall be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction

Notices to terminate tenancy can only be served on the tenant after the landlord files the Declaration with LAHD, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after it is served

At the landlord's sole discretion and cost, the landlord may elect to pay the monetary relocation benefits through an escrow account. The monies must be placed in the escrow account within the required 15-day period

Payments from the escrow account shall be made within three (3) working days of receiving a payment request. The remaining balance of the escrow account shall be disbursed upon certification of the vacation of the rental housing unit

rule.title: Relocation Assistance Amounts for Eligible and Qualified Tenants (Standard)
rule.requirement: Relocation assistance amounts depend on tenant classification (eligible vs. qualified), length of tenancy, and income. Eligible households with less than 3 years tenancy: $11,000; with 3+ years or low income (≤80% AMI): $14,400. Qualified households with less than 3 years: $23,150; with 3+ years or low income: $27,400. Amounts apply per unit and increase every July 1st.
rule.citation: LAMC 151.09.E, 165.06.A; Chart A Relocation Assistance Amounts
rule.quoted_span: Chart A: Relocation Assistance Amounts Effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 Eligible Household $11,000 $14,400 Qualified Household $23,150 $27,400 Increases every July 1st. The relocation amounts above apply if a tenant is displaced for a no-fault reason described on page 1 of this bulletin.
rule.coverage_conditions: Eligible or Qualified tenant status; tenancy length; income at or below 80% AMI; unit subject to RSO or JCO; no-fault eviction not for demolition for new construction
rule.exemptions: Mom & Pop properties (owner/family occupancy only) pay reduced amounts; single-family dwellings owned by natural persons (JCO only) pay one month's rent instead

rule.title: Relocation Assistance for Mom & Pop Properties (Reduced Amounts)
rule.requirement: Mom & Pop properties may pay reduced relocation assistance for owner or family occupancy evictions if: (1) building has 4 or fewer rental units; (2) landlord has not utilized this provision in prior 3 years; (3) landlord owns no more than 4 residential units plus single-family home on separate lot in Los Angeles; (4) eligible relative does not own residential property in Los Angeles. Reduced amounts: Eligible households $10,550; Qualified households $21,250.

The reduced fee for Mom and Pop properties applies only for evictions for occupancy by the owner or an eligible relative and only if all of the following conditions exist: 1. The landlord owns no more than four units of residential property and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City of Los Angeles; and 4. Any eligible relative for whom the landlord is recovering possession of the rental unit does not own residential property in the City of Los Angeles. rule.title: Relocation Assistance for Single-Family Dwellings Owned by Natural Persons (JCO)
rule.requirement: When residential property is a single-family dwelling subject to JCO and owner is a natural person (including trusts or registered legal entities controlled by that person) who owns no more than 4 dwelling units and single-family home on separate lot in Los Angeles, relocation assistance is one month's rent in effect when written notice was served, as monetary payment or credit. LAMC 151.30(E) does not apply.

The Los Angeles Municipal Code Section 151.30(E) shall not apply. (LAMC 165.06.A.(6)).

rule.title: Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) - Demolition for New Construction
rule.requirement: Resident Protections Ordinance effective February 11, 2025 applies to Protected Units demolished for new construction. Landlord must file Declaration of Intent to Evict (JCO units) or Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental Housing Use (RSO units) with LAHD. Pay relocation assistance per HCA or City law, whichever is higher. Three options: (1) Standardized Payment via City Consultant; (2) Comparable Replacement Unit + RSO/JCO relocation; (3) Individualized Relocation via private consultant. Failure to comply results in penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of permit clearances.
rule.citation: LAMC Sections 165.03.I(1); California Government Code Sections 66300 et seq. (HCA); Ordinances #188481, #188482
rule.quoted_span: On February 11, 2025, the Los Angeles City Council adopted the RPO which codified and expanded upon replacement requirements and occupant protections of the HCA, and enhanced requirements for Restricted Affordable Units. The RPO only applies to Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction. Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to comply with relocation requirements under the RPO. Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rule.coverage_conditions: Protected Units (RSO units, rent-controlled units, units rented by lower/very low income households within past 5 years, or units withdrawn under Ellis Act within past 10 years); demolished for new construction; Notice of Intent filed with LAHD
rule.sanctions: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit; withholding of LAHD permit clearances

field_evidence.quoted_span: On February 11, 2025, the Los Angeles City Council adopted the RPO
The RPO only applies to Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction

landlord must file Declaration of Intent to Evict for units regulated by the JCO per the Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC) Section 165.03.I(1) or file with LAHD a Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental Housing Use for units regulated by the RSO
Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances

Protected Units: (1) Residential dwelling units that are or were subject to a recorded covenant, ordinance, or law that restricts rents to levels affordable to persons and families of lower or very low income within the past five years. (2) Residential dwelling units that are or were subject to any form of rent or price control through a public entity's valid exercise of its police power within the past five years. This includes all RSO units. (3) Residential dwelling units that are or were rented by lower or very low income households within the past five years. (4) Residential dwelling units that were withdrawn from rent or lease in accordance the Ellis Act within the past 10 years.

rule.title: RPO Option 3 - Individualized Relocation for Demolition for New Construction
rule.requirement: Under RPO Option 3, owner must provide approval letter from LAHD Housing Development Bureau approving relocation plan and private relocation consultant in compliance with State law. rule.title: RPO Occupant Protections and Rights
rule.requirement: Resident Protections Ordinance provides occupant protections including: (1) Right to Relocation; (2) Right to Remain in unit up to 6 months prior to start of construction activities, including 6-month notice to move out; (3) Right to Return to same unit if demolition does not proceed; (4) Right of First Refusal to new building for some tenants; (5) Tenant Notification Requirements. For more details, see Los Angeles City Planning Department website and Fact Sheet: Replacement Unit Requirements and Occupant Protections.
rule.citation: RPO per Ordinances #188481, #188482, LAMC 165.03.I(1); California Government Code Section 66300 et seq.
rule.quoted_span: The RPO's occupant protections include: 1) Right to Relocation, 2) Right to Remain in the unit up to 6 months prior to start of construction activities, which includes a 6-month notice to move out, 3) Right to Return to the same unit if the demolition does not proceed, 4) Right of First Refusal to the new building for some tenants and 5) Tenant Notification Requirements.

rule.title: Tenant Remedies for Non-Payment of Relocation Assistance
rule.requirement: Tenant may raise failure of landlord to provide relocation assistance as affirmative defense in landlord's action to recover possession. Tenant may file complaint with LAHD online at housing.lacity.gov/residents/file-a-rso-complaint or call (866) 557-7368. Tenant may seek private right of action by obtaining legal advice. For escrow disputes between account holder, tenant, and owner regarding fund release, dispute notice must be sent to LAHD by escrow holder with copy of escrow instructions.
rule.quoted_span: In an action by the landlord to recover possession of a rental unit, the tenant may raise as an affirmative defense the failure of the landlord to provide relocation assistance. A tenant may file a complaint with LAHD online at https://housing.lacity.gov/residents/file-a-rso-complaint or call the general hotline at (866) 557-7368. A tenant may seek a private right of action by obtaining legal advice. Where there is an escrow dispute between the escrow account holder, tenant, and owner about the release of deposited funds, a dispute notice must be sent to the LAHD by the escrow holder. A copy of the escrow instructions given to the tenant must accompany the notice.
rule.coverage_conditions: Landlord failed to pay relocation assistance; tenant in possession action or seeking remedy for non-payment
rule.sanctions: Affirmative defense to possession action; LAHD complaint and enforcement; private right of action; escrow dispute resolution process
